messages:
oliver: Heads-up - onboarding run for v2-mini-ptq shows a weird class of funcall parse failures: the model sometimes glues a leading punctuation onto the tool name, so our strict matcher misses it and parser falls back to raw-text handling.
tia: saw a handful of examples. sample from canary: ```json
{
  \"tool\": \"-lookup_user\",
  \"args\": \"{\\\"id\\\": \\\"u_17\\\", \\\"limit\\\": 5}\"
}
```
kelly: Oof. Our tool-dispatcher expects tool name to match ^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$ so the leading '-' causes a miss and then the args blob never gets extracted. That leads to the retry budget kicking in and duplicate calls.
sam: I also found examples where a truncated args string lost the opening brace: ```json
{
  \"tool\": \"update_profile\",
  \"args\": \"\"name\\\": \\\"Maya\\\"}\"
}
```
sam: parser errors on the malformed JSON; retry replayed the same fragment, creating two partial updates (race) for one customer. ops-bot: incident-alert: duplicate partial updates observed (customer: gamma-sys) - flagged for manual rollback.
oliver: short-term mitigations proposed: 1) a tolerant tool-name matcher that strips a small set of leading punctuation before matching (configurable toggle), 2) a pre-parse args sanity step that rejects obviously-truncated blobs and attempts small, auditable repairs (e.g., insert missing leading `{`), 3) dedupe identical inferred tool invocations within a single LLM response.
tia: +1 for dedupe. For the repair heuristics, let's keep a strict logging mode that stores original+attempted-repair to S3 so we can inspect whether fixes hide a model regression.
kelly: long-term: add a token-boundary parity test to PTQ onboarding. For every golden prompt, run fp16 vs ptq and assert tokenization boundaries for tool-name and opening `{"` tokens are preserved. Fail PTQ builds that increase boundary-mismatch rate > 0.1%.
ci-bot: queued: `ptq-token-boundary-check` against v2-mini-ptq canary set  ETA ~25m.
infra-bot: note: enabling tolerant tool-name matcher requires a small opconfig rollout. Will schedule a 1% sampling window first.
oliver: PR incoming for tolerant matcher + dedupe gate (will be opt-in): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4902. Includes telemetry counters: tool_name_normalized, args_repair_attempted, dedupe_dropped.
sam: also adding stronger idempotency tokens in dispatcher - if two tool payloads are byte-for-byte identical and occur within same response window, only deliver once and emit a warning event.
ops-bot: customer-alert: duplicate partial updates reduced after 1% tolerant matcher + dedupe sampling. Continuing monitoring.
tia: follow-ups: (A) land sanitizer/dedupe as opt-in canary (oliver, sam), (B) add token-boundary asserts to PTQ CI (kelly + ci-bot), (C) backfill failing canary samples into token-diff dashboard for triage (infra-bot).
oliver: will open the small runbook for oncall on how to abort retries and revoke partial updates if we see dupes in prod.
ci-bot: `ptq-token-boundary-check` job finished - report uploaded: s3://redwood-canary-reports/5812345678/token-boundary-report.html
kelly: report shows 14 boundary mismatches out of 12000 samples (~0.117%), above the 0.1% threshold. We'll hold this PTQ variant from wider rollout until we either adjust quantization or extend tokenizer protections.
sam: good catch. locking the canary variant and escalating to quant-team for model-level debug.
ops-bot: incident status: canary-level; no customer-wide rollback necessary.
oliver: thanks all. tracking next steps in epic `E-ptq-toolcall-boundary` and will loop in quant-team.
